_README: OPS-LAMBDACONFIG-001 — the repo's declaration of prod Lambda configuration.
Enforced by scripts/check-lambda-config.py, which deploy-lambda.yml's verify-daily-plan job
runs against the LIVE account after every prod deploy. A mismatch fails the run.
WHY: on 2026-08-17 CARE_WATER_LEDGER_ENABLED and CARE_RAIN_MAXDAYS_ENABLED were found ABSENT
(not false) from garden-daily-plan, so RAIN_DEPTH — ~140 lines, fully unit-tested — was
unreachable in prod while CI stayed green either way. Nothing in the repo asserted prod flag
state, so a code comment claiming a flag was on was the only 'source'. Absent and false behave
identically at a === 'true' gate but mean different things, so this file distinguishes them.
The same deploy also revealed garden-plants living at 1024MB with the repo declaring nothing.
SCHEMA — per function name (the live name, e.g. 'garden-plants'):
memory   int    required MemorySize in MB
timeout  int    required Timeout in seconds (optional; omit to not assert)
env      obj    per-KEY expectation. NOT exhaustive — unlisted keys are ignored, which is
deliberate: SECRET_REFRESH / FORCE_COLD_START are operational churn.
ENV VALUE SENTINELS — type-encoded so they can never collide with a real value (always a string):
null      key MUST BE ABSENT from the live map. This is the absent-vs-false distinction.
true      key MUST BE PRESENT with any value. For values that are environment-derived or
not worth pinning (Clerk subs, SNS ARNs). Proves 'not wiped' without hardcoding.
"string"  key MUST BE PRESENT and equal exactly.
FLIPPING A FLAG IS A REPO CHANGE. Editing this file is how a flag flip becomes reviewable;
flipping live without editing here fails the next deploy. That is the point, not a nuisance.
Use scripts/lambda-env-set.sh for the live write — never a bare --environment (set-not-merge).
Captured from live us-east-1 on 2026-08-18. Values are CURRENT REALITY, not aspiration.
URL / CORS AND EVENTBRIDGE (added 2026-08-30, OPS-DEPLOYCOESILENT-001).
deploy-lambda.yml carries 15 continue-on-error steps. An audit classified all 15: TEN write only
Lambda env, and every key they set is declared below, so the env assertions already turn their
silent failure into a red deploy. The other FIVE write resources this manifest could not see -
Function URL creation, CORS restore, and three EventBridge cron rules - so their failure was
silent end to end. A0.3 above verifies exactly ONE rule (garden-daily-plan-nightly, hardcoded),
so the two INTRADAY rules that move the Today watering verdict, and xp-reconcile, had no check
at all. The fix is NOT removing continue-on-error: those steps are fail-soft because the deploy
role may lack a permission, and hard-failing there would red a deploy over something unrelated to
the code. Asserting the RESULT keeps the soft failure and removes the silence.
url   per function. SENTINELS MIRROR env:
null                          -> the function MUST NOT have a Function URL. Correct for
the event-driven three (daily-plan, photocdn-derivative,
xp-reconcile); catches one silently gaining a public
HTTP entry point.
{"cors_origins": [...]}       -> MUST have a URL, with exactly these AllowOrigins.
Order-insensitive. This is the L-097 guard: a deploy
clobbering CORS breaks the browser app while every job
stays green, and smoke-prod.py asserts no CORS at all.
{}                            -> MUST have a URL; origins unasserted.
key absent                    -> asserts nothing (same non-exhaustive rule as env).
eventbridge   TOP-LEVEL, not a function. A list of {name, state?, targets?}. Absent optional
keys assert nothing. targets matters on its own: a rule that exists but has zero
targets fires into nothing, and describe-rule alone cannot show that.
NOTE this key is reserved in check-lambda-config.py (RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL) so that
load_manifest() keeps returning FUNCTIONS ONLY.

garden-daily-plan._note: memory INTENTIONALLY 256 — DRG-NIGHTLYTIMEOUT-001 proved I/O wait, not CPU. env below is the COMPLETE set of vars lambda/daily-plan reads, so every flag is declared present-or-absent.

garden-plants._note: OPS-PLANTSLAMBDACPU-001 — bumped 256->1024 live 2026-08-17 with Dave's approval: ~446 HMAC CDN presigns per list request were CPU-bound at 256MB's 0.145 vCPU. update-function-code does not touch memory, so the bump survives deploys, but it was UNDECLARED until now.

garden-inventory-items._note: V4-SEEDINV-001 — Anthropic image-OCR proxy needs >30s and base64 headroom.

garden-facebook-share._note: V4-FBSHARE-001. FB_SHARE_ENABLED='1' since 2026-08-21 — Facebook posting is LIVE (secret provisioned, token non-expiring, Dev-mode post visibility verified equal to a hand-made post). This line declares that deliberate flip so the drift guard stops redding every promote on it. 1024MB/180s (was 512/60): the live function was raised to these values on 2026-08-21 because it fans out over up to 10 photos — S3 get + metadata strip + a multipart Graph upload each — and a timeout mid-Promise.all orphans uploaded Graph media with NO cleanup, because the catch never runs. deploy-lambda.yml hardcoded the old 60/512 with no read/compare, so every Lambda deploy silently reverted that raise; fixed in the same commit as this line. IG_SHARE_ENABLED is declared '1' and Instagram is LIVE — see the ENABLEMENT paragraph at the end of this note, which is the authorising record. It was declared ABSENT until 2026-08-30, for two successive reasons: first because the handler did not exist, then (from 2026-08-28) because it was the one control keeping a built, deployable publish path dark. That history is kept because the tripwire below only means anything if you can see what it was guarding. POST /api/share/instagram is routed and reachable the moment this key is set to '1' — there is no second gate behind it, and an Instagram post CANNOT be deleted through the API. Setting it is therefore a SHIP EVENT, not a config tweak, and must be a deliberate act with the same weight as a promote. If this key's live value ever CHANGES — set, cleared, or altered — without an accompanying edit to this line, treat it as an unauthorised change rather than drift. That guard was written when the key was absent and said 'appears'; it is restated for a key that is now set, and it is deliberately NOT weakened by the enablement having happened. IG_STAGING_BUCKET added 2026-08-30: the Instagram flow parks an EXIF-stripped scratch copy of a private photo before handing Meta a presigned URL, and it used to park it in garden-photos-prod — which is versioned AND replicates every object to garden-photos-replica-usw2 with delete-marker replication disabled. Since S3 never replicates version-specific deletes, NO deletion of any kind reached the replica and every staged copy accumulated in us-west-2 permanently. garden-photos-derivatives-769788341849 is unversioned and unreplicated (both verified live), so a plain DeleteObject genuinely deletes and there is no second region. The handler FALLS BACK to S3_PHOTOS_BUCKET when this key is absent, so it is safe to deploy ahead of the key — but the fallback is the old, leaky behaviour, which is why this is asserted as an exact string rather than left optional. ENABLEMENT 2026-08-30: IG_SHARE_ENABLED flipped null -> '1' on Dave's explicit instruction to make Instagram fully functional. This edit IS the accompanying repo change this line demands - the key appearing live without it would have been an unauthorised enablement. Preconditions verified live the same day, not recalled: the Page-linked Instagram business account is 17841480663170931 (gardensatmathews) and matches the secret; the page_token is valid, type PAGE, expires_at 0; the deployed prod bundle carries the Instagram route; and the whole publish path was exercised end to end against an unpublished staging Page (share_log status posted, 7.7s). NOTE the frontend half is a SEPARATE and deliberately withheld switch: api.js routes BOTH /api/share/facebook and /api/share/instagram through VITE_API_FACEBOOK_SHARE, so setting that repo variable turns on Facebook posting - which is already armed - in the same instant. Instagram cannot be enabled in the UI alone as the code stands.

garden-photocdn-derivative._note: Created by infra/photocdn.yaml (CFN), not by deploy-lambda.yml's create branch — which would produce nodejs20.x/x86_64/256MB. Asserted here so a CFN placeholder-revert is caught by the deploy rather than days later.
